To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have shown that a calibration of the GLAS signal with field measurements allows a better prediction of the AGB in French Guiana.
a calibrated regression method with GLAS data and spatial and environmental variables allows us to produce AGB maps with high precision for high AGB (>300 Mg/ha).
a calibrated regression approach with a combination of GLAS, forest inventory and environmental variables can predict AGB with good precision for high AGB levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the use of GLAS data to map high AGB values, (2) the calibration of regression models with field data to improve the estimation of high AGB values and (3) the use of spatial and environmental variables to improve the estimation and prediction of high AGB.
the calibration of remote-sensing data to improve the estimation of high AGB values, which are not represented by the existing global maps.
the development of a calibrated model to map AGB at a regional scale in the context of the lack of data and the saturation and dilution bias in remote-sensing data for AGB mapping.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of remote sensing and forest inventory data, with a calibrated regression model, is a good way to predict high AGB values and to map the spatial variation of AGB at regional and global levels.
the combination of optical, radar and environmental data can be used to map AGB at the regional scale with good precision.
the combination of GLAS and field data is the best option to produce AGB maps for French Guiana, and probably for the whole tropical region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an approach for mapping AGB at the local scale by using remote sensing and environmental data.
the calibrated regression model based in GLAS with dependent variables can produce good ACG estimates even for high values if the calibration dataset fit the AGB ranges.
the combination of GLAS data and environmental variables can be a powerful tool for mapping forest AGB at regional and global levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the calibration of global models for high AGB is possible, but it requires a better understanding of the limits and potentialities of the data and of the models.
a calibrated regression approach can provide a better understanding of the AGB distribution in tropical forests and improve the estimation of AGB in the range of high AGB values.
we can produce high-precision and high-coverage AGB maps for tropical forests with a calibrated regression model that uses GLAS data as a reference for AGB values.
